newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Deadlock continues in Bangladesh prison revolt.
newsitem.headline: Deadlock continues in Bangladesh prison revolt.

text.p: Nearly 2,000 armed police and para-military troops were on Thursday guarding a Bangladesh jail in western Jessore where prisoners continued to defy a government plea to end their five days of revolt, police said.

"We are ready for a raid but political leaders are still insiting on a peaceful end to the crisis," one police official at Jessore, 270 kilomteres (160 miles) west of capital Dhaka, told Reuters on telephone.

The police said an intense negotiation with the prisoners through loudspeakers had apparently failed after they refused to allow prison gurads inside. "We want no one here but the home minister," one police official quoted the prisoners as saying.
A personal staff of Home (interior) Minister rafiqul Islam said in Dhaka Islam was still not planning to go to Jessore.
Prisoners, angered by being left out of an independence day amnesty, took control of Jessore jail on Monday after scaring away guards with iron bars and knives.
Witnesses said the authorities mobilised bulldozers, water cannons and ladders around the jail compound at the town centre.
"It seems they (police) are preparing for a raid," said one local journalist.
The authorities on Wednesday called in extra troops from nearby districts and restricted on movement of public within 200 yards of the jail.
Anxious relatives of jail inmates were trying to get near to the prison which holds about 3,000 prisoners, some convicts and others on remand.
"We are very anxious about the safety of some 300 female prisoners," said one jail official on Wednesday.
The trouble started after 90 prisoners were freed nationwide under an amnesty awarded as part of Monday's 25th independence anniversary celebrations.
Some were demanding freedom while others sought better food and treatment.
Jail officials said the prison had food stocks for two weeks. REUTER SA SAZ
